findings: The current Dutch public page lists Work and Organizational Psychology first. The previous Clinical-first statement was copied from the English target and is false for this exact page. The generic Dutch target names no default major, so the existing official-order tie-break now selects Work and Organizational Psychology. The adopted Dutch table lists the same four six-credit major units and explicitly identifies English as their teaching language.

The Dutch curriculum has thirteen first-year units totalling sixty EC, ten common second-year units totalling forty-two and three six-credit major units. Work Psychology is offered in block two, Organizational Psychology in block three and Diversity and Inclusion at Work in block four. Applied Work and Organizational Psychology is the third-year block-one practical unit. With thirty open credits, Applied Methods and Statistics, Philosophy of Science and the twelve-credit Work/Organizational thesis, year three totals sixty.

The Dutch appendix requires all first-year courses and sixty post-propaedeutic EC before thesis entry. The specific 550012-B-12 thesis entry confirms at least 120 EC including the first year and experimental-subject hours for September and recommends 138 EC for February. Full completion of the preceding two years satisfies the rule. Quantitative research is illustrated; qualitative and systematic-review variants are subject to the appendix’s three-credit methods-elective condition before submission.

Dutch Academic Skills B requires passing A; A is completed before B in the published first-year order. Skills C contains information-literacy and plagiarism tests and twenty experimental-subject hours. The older zero-credit subject-hours route and the older three-credit Skills B apply to earlier cohorts, not this 2026 three/two/one-credit structure. GROW is zero credit and not added. Group Skills and Communication Skills entries impose no earlier-course condition but require timely enrolment and their actual coursework.

The major descriptions distinguish individual work experiences, personnel selection, training and motivation; organisational attitudes, teams, leadership and change; diversity, belonging and inclusion; and the applied PATHS intervention model. The applied course has group presentations, individual logs, feedback and attendance requirements, including no more than one absence unless an exception is approved. It is not an internship. The major’s first two courses expressly require no prior specialist knowledge.

The Dutch open-space rule differs from the English version’s broad psychology-related phrasing: at least twelve of thirty EC must come from non-selected psychology majors or predefined psychology electives; the remaining eighteen are free. Deviating from that rule requires prior Examination Board approval. No particular minor, elective, host or placement is assumed.

sharedResearchReuse.scope: Shared 2026 general TSB regulations and course-relevance research remain valid. The current appendix was retrieved again and its Dutch sections and exact-target course entries were inspected independently. English target curriculum/major approval is not transferred.
